The '''PIP/2 systems control droid''' was produced by [[Genetech Corporation]] with the intention to replace organic operators running control boards. It was advertised as glitch-proof, and was heavily hyped, but failed miserably. Although it handled simple tasks with ease, it was unable to handle excessive stimuli, such as bells or flashing lights, constantly malfunctioning. Genetech quickly responded to complaints and recalled as many of these [[Droid/Legends|droids]] as possible. These recalled droids were given programming patches, and operated almost perfectly. It was not enough, however, as the droid was discontinued after two [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

==Description==
The PIP/2 was designed to be installed in the center of a wraparound control desk, capable of operating multiple stations at the same time. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] had a rounded, spherical head where its [[Droid brain/Legends|multi-tasking cognitive processor]] was housed. [[Photoreceptor/Legends|Optical sensors]] were mounted around the head, spaced evenly every thirty-six degrees to give the droid a full three-hundred-and-sixty degrees of vision. The head was crowned by a unit that had two rotating reception antennae, and two more optical sensors that were dedicated to dealing with organics and supervisors.<ref name="FF109" />

The droid's design was likened to a multi-[[Limb/Legends|armed]] sea creature with the torso of the PIP/2 being a thin, spindly, core with eight articulated [[Manipulator arm/Legends|control limbs]] attached just below the droid's head. Each arm terminated in a hand with a number of dextrous fighters that were used to manipulate buttons and controls. The PIP/2 had four variable-height telescoping legs that could bunch up, allowing the droid to fit into tighter spaces in the center of the control desk.<ref name="FF109" />

==History==
[[Genetech Corporation]] manufactured a number of successful [[Supervisor droid/Legends|supervisor]] and [[Administrative droid/Legends|administrative droids]], and their market research identified a potentially untapped niche opportunity in the field of control-board operation.<ref name="EGTD" /> While it was acknowledged as a potentially small gap in the market, the droid market was extremely competitive and any opportunity had to be taken seriously.<ref name="FF109" /> Although a number of modern [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems were built with [[Microprocessor/Legends|microprocessors]] and integrated [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]], a large amount of computer networks still relied on older input systems such as keyboards and central switchboards.<ref name="EGTD" /> Networks still relying on these control systems included air traffic control and municipal works such as [[Water/Legends|water]] supply companies.<ref name="FF109" />

These systems were handled by organic operators for a number of reasons, ranging from cost and convenience, to security considerations. These operators often became overworked due to the stress and anxiety<ref name="EGTD" /> of the jobs which often led to serious errors being made that resulted in the companies involved having to spend large amounts of money to correct the foul-ups.<ref name="FF109" /> Seeing the potential in replacing these workers with automated droids that could work faster and without making mistakes, Geentech Corporation rushed the PIP/2 into development despite the market for the droid being a relatively small one. The company invested a significant amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] into the line's creation.<ref name="EGTD" />

By the time that the PIP/2 was ready to be released onto the market, the project had been hit by a number of logistical delays resulting in the company and the stockholders having to rely on the droid selling in record numbers to recoup their investment. In short, if the PIP/2 did not sell well, the entire fiscal [[Standard year/Legends|year]] would be considered a disaster. Genetech advertised the PIP/2 as "glitch-proof", offering money-back guarantees to all buyers from the municipal and corporate sectors.<ref name="EGTD" /> Initially, the droid sold well despite the limited market it was designed to cater to.<ref name="FF109" /> Unfortunately for the company, the PIP/2 began to glitch,<ref name="EGTD" /> and fall prey to the same issues that organic operators had.<ref name="FF109" /> 

While the [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brain]] could handle simple tasks, it soon became overtaxed when exposed to stimuli such as alarms and warning indicators. Overwhelmed PIP/2s resorted to either shutting down completely, or inputting the wrong commands as it attempted to keep up. On one occasion, a PIP/2 working in a [[habitation sphere]] cross-wired the sewage drains with the [[Water/Legends|water]] pipes. One thousand and thirteen cases of severe intestinal distress were reported by the sphere's inhabitants.<ref name="EGTD" /> Another incidents resulted in air traffic chaos and pandemonium.<ref name="FF109" />

Genetech was quick to respond to the number of complaints from buyers, recalling them and installing new programming patches into the units. While these modified droids operated perfectly, the reputational damage was done<ref name="EGTD" /> and buyers were wary to invest in the droid after its public failures.<ref name="FF109" /> The line was discontinued within two years. It was such an expensive failure that it ended Genetech's run of successful droid releases, and forced the company to make a temporary return to producing medical supplies and focusing on its core medical market as it waited for the public to forget about the PIP/2.<ref name="EGTD" />

The droids continued to see use, and the [[Holographic Zoo of Extinct Animals]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] used a PIP/2 to control [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] dioramas, as well as for keeping visitors moving through the exhibit halls. Unfortunately for the droid, it had an "unpleasant" encounter with an enraged [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] after [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]] and [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] became lost in the [[Museum/Legends|museum]].<ref name="EGTD" />
